meta.title: A Stamp for Aunt Sue
meta.textType: story: sending a drawing, with prices and a note

paragraphs: Lily drew a lovely picture for Aunt Sue in Chiang Mai. It showed the family and Pip. "Aunt Sue is far away," said Lily, "so I will send it by post." She decided to write a short letter too. The letter said, "For Aunt Sue. From Lily." She put the letter and the picture in a big envelope. On Saturday, Tom and Dad went to the post office with her. Pip came too.

They walked past the police station and across the railway bridge. The traffic was noisy, so Tom held Pip's lead. Many cars and buses went along the street. "Hurry, please," said Dad. "Do you have the envelope, Lily?" asked Dad. "Yes, I have it," said Lily. The journey took ten minutes. They arrived early and waited at the door. The post office was small and bright. Tom looked at the postcards on the wall.

At the post office, Lily asked, "How much is a stamp?" A woman at the counter smiled at Lily. The woman said, "A stamp for Chiang Mai is fifteen baht." Lily had twenty baht, so she got five baht in change. She put the stamp on the envelope. "I can write the address," said Lily, "but I can't reach the box!" Tom lifted her up to the red post box.

Lily was putting the envelope through the hole when Pip said, "Woof!" The envelope went through. Aunt Sue will get it soon. "Well done!" shouted Dad. "Thank you, Tom," said Lily. "You're welcome," said Tom. Lily spent fifteen baht and saved five baht. "I will draw another picture tomorrow," she said. Lily was excited, and they walked home together.
